nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$ and a finite list $W = (W_0, \dots, W_{m-1})$ of Boolean functions on $n$ variables, the concatenation of $W$ on $n + k$ variables takes the value $W_0(\mathrm{false}, \dots, \mathrm{false})$ at the all-false input when $W$ is nonempty, and the value false when $W$ is empty.

nodes.summary: Let $f$ and $g$ be monotone Boolean functions on $n$ variables, ordered pointwise, with duals $f^*$ and $g^*$. If $f \le g$ then $g^* \le f^*$. Moreover $(f \lor g)^* = f^* \land g^*$ and $(f \land g)^* = f^* \lor g^*$, where $\lor$ and $\land$ are pointwise disjunction and conjunction.
nodes.title: Duality reverses order and exchanges joins and meets

nodes.summary: For every $n$ and every Boolean function $f \colon \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$, writing $f^\star$ for the dual of $f$, we have $(f^\star)^\star = f$.
nodes.title: Duality of Boolean functions is an involution

nodes.summary: For a Boolean function $f \colon \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$, its dual is the Boolean function $f^\star \colon \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ given by $f^\star(x) = \lnot f(\bar x)$, where $\bar x$ is the coordinatewise complement of $x$.
nodes.title: Dual of a Boolean function

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a Boolean function on $n$ variables, let $\pi$ be a permutation of the $n$ coordinates, and let $f^\pi$ be the function $x \mapsto f(x \circ \pi)$. If $f$ is monotone, then $f^\pi$ is monotone and $(f^*)^\pi = (f^\pi)^*$, where $f^*$ is the dual of $f$. If $f$ is self-dual monotone, then so is $f^\pi$.
nodes.title: Permuting variables preserves monotonicity, duals and self-duality

nodes.summary: For every $n$ and every Boolean vector $x \in \{0,1\}^n$, writing $\bar x$ for the coordinatewise complement of $x$, we have $\bar{\bar x} = x$.
nodes.title: Complementation of Boolean vectors is an involution

nodes.summary: The complement of a Boolean vector $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ is the vector $\bar x \in \{0,1\}^n$ obtained by negating every coordinate: $\bar x_i = \lnot x_i$ for every $i < n$.
nodes.title: Complement of a Boolean vector

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be odd and let $\pi$ be a permutation of the $n$ coordinates. Then there is a self-dual monotone Boolean function $f$ on $n$ variables with $f(x \circ \pi) = f(x)$ for every input $x$.
nodes.title: For odd $n$, every permutation fixes a self-dual monotone function

nodes.summary: A Boolean function $f \colon \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ is self-dual monotone when it is monotone, that is, $f(x) \le f(y)$ for all $x, y \in \{0,1\}^n$ with $x_i \le y_i$ for every $i < n$, and it equals its dual, that is, $f = f^\star$, where $f^\star(x) = \lnot f(\bar x)$ and $\bar x$ is the coordinatewise complement of $x$.
nodes.title: Self-dual monotone Boolean functions

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, let $d_n$ be the number of monotone Boolean functions $\{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ (for the coordinatewise order with $0 < 1$) and let $\lambda_{n+2}$ be the number of self-dual monotone Boolean functions $\{0,1\}^{n+2} \to \{0,1\}$, that is, monotone functions $f$ with $f(\bar x) = \lnot f(x)$ for every $x$, where $\bar x$ is the coordinatewise complement of $x$. Then $d_n \le \lambda_{n+2}$.
nodes.title: Dedekind numbers bound self-dual counts from below (Corollary 11)

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $\mathcal U$ be a maximal intersecting family of subsets of $X = \{0, \dots, n-1\}$: any two members of $\mathcal U$, not necessarily distinct, have nonempty intersection, and no family of subsets of $X$ strictly containing $\mathcal U$ has this property. Then for every $A \subseteq X$, $A \in \mathcal U$ if and only if $X \setminus A \notin \mathcal U$.

Then for all natural numbers $n$ and $k$, $D_{n+k}$ is order-isomorphic to the poset of monotone maps $\{0,1\}^k \to D_n$, ordered pointwise.

Combinatorics

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
